Definition: to be (causative, make) long (literally or figuratively)
BiblicalUsage: The word means to be long, and it carries the promise of long days. Honour your father and mother, that your days may be long on the land; a man's discretion makes him slow to anger; and the Servant, having made His soul an offering for sin, shall prolong His days and see His seed.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe long life is not a reward for being lucky, it is the fruit of honour and patience. The longest life of all belongs to the Servant who died and yet prolongs His days forever.
